summary: Plausible observations of an atmospheric reentry.
description: Observations on December 10, 1991 in the evening by witnesses located in the Hautes Pyrénées and in Gironde of a luminous phenomenon whose characteristics suggest an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Likely observations of a large-scale atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 28, 1991, at approximately 10:30 PM, at least 25 witnesses spread across the Atlantic coast and southwestern France saw a very bright green sphere moving silently at high speed for about ten seconds. According to some accounts, this sphere disintegrated in a shower of sparks. The general direction deduced from the accounts appears to be southeast to northwest. It is highly likely that this was the atmospheric reentry of space debris.

summary: Successive observations of a bright point in the sky: observation of Venus.
description: This observation, previously published under the name BRIEY (54) with a classification of "B" (probable sighting of a celestial body), was re-analyzed in 2009. Between October 20th and 24th, 1991, between 6 and 8 AM, two witnesses were intrigued by the presence of a luminous phenomenon in the sky. One of the witnesses filmed the appearances of this very bright point with his camcorder. The police also noted the presence of a luminous point in the same location in the sky. When filming with maximum zoom, a sphere with two "notches" appeared: this turned out to be a problem with the camcorder lens. Following astronomical verification, the investigation revealed that the "evening star" (or "Morning Star") was indeed visible in this area of the sky on the dates indicated and that it was at its brightest, with a magnitude reaching -4.46 during this period. In view of the additional investigation, GEIPAN classifies this case "A" as perfectly identified: successive observations of the planet Venus.

summary: Observations by numerous witnesses of a probable large-scale atmospheric reentry.
description: On October 10, 1991, at approximately 9:30 PM, numerous witnesses throughout the departments of southwestern France observed a very bright white glow for a few seconds. The glow moved very rapidly, leaving a significant trail, generally in a north-south direction. Some witnesses also heard a loud explosion accompanying the phenomenon. An article in the local newspaper prompted many witnesses to come forward. The characteristics of the observation support the hypothesis of a large-scale atmospheric reentry, likely of natural origin given the observed direction.

summary: Observations of an intense, static white light in the sky: mistaken for Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, originally classified as type C, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This particular case study was classified as type C in 1991 by SEPRA and was previously named Cournon-d'Auvergne (63) after the gendarmerie brigade. On September 19, 1991, at 5:25 a.m., the gendarmerie in Cournon d'Auvergne (63) was notified by a witness residing in Clermont-Ferrand (63) of the presence of a bright point in the sky. The gendarme on duty managed to observe the UFO. A second anonymous witness contacted the gendarmerie at 5:30 a.m. to report the presence of the UFO, and a third call at 5:40 a.m. from the Clermont-Ferrand police station confirmed the events. The UFO was described as having the appearance of a large star, emitting a strong white light. The apparent size of the UFO was very small, as it was compared to a bright point. Observation with binoculars revealed no details. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: the planet Venus. Furthermore, this planet was clearly visible and of high magnitude in the observed area of the sky, yet the witnesses made no mention of it. The issue is not the witnesses' visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (astonishment, fatigue, nighttime observation). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of a weak anomaly is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misidentification of the planet Venus.

summary: Observation of the passage of two red dots and one white dot in a triangle: lack of information.
description: On September 5, 1991, at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness observed three luminous points in a triangle, pointing backward, twice, 15 minutes apart. The points were two red points forward and one white point backward, following the direction of movement. The speed was slow and the movement silent. No other information was available regarding this observation.

summary: Observation of the passage of a large, round object.
description: Recent report (July 31, 2009) of an earlier sighting (September 1990 or 1991; the witness no longer remembers the exact date). A witness recounts observing, at dusk, the slow movement of a large circular object (between 20 and 40 meters) that emitted a regular rumbling sound. For 3 to 4 minutes, this person saw flashing lights of various colors around the object's perimeter. The object followed a straight NE-SW trajectory at an altitude of between 100 and 200 meters. The object disappeared without changing its trajectory, blending into the sky. The witness filed a report with the local police. No other reports have been collected regarding this phenomenon. The age of the sighting makes any investigation difficult, if not impossible. Following a new letter from the witness (dated September 14, 2010), he specifies the date of observation, which becomes September 1991 (no precision on the day), and attaches documents on the trajectory taken by the object as well as a schematic representation he made of the observed object (see witness letter).

On August 20, 1991, at approximately 5:30 a.m., two gendarmes on patrol briefly observed a very bright, bluish sphere moving at high speed and leaving a significant trail of sparks. No other witnesses were found, but the phenomenon described resembled a natural or artificial atmospheric reentry.

summary: Reported testimonies of multiple observations made by children of a blue luminous mass with lights of various colours and flashes in the night sky: lack of reliable information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as C, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On August 18, 1991, a ufologist went to the Gendarmerie to report a sighting he had heard the previous day. This sighting was made by a group of five children (aged 7 to 10) in Gilette on August 16, 1991, after 11:00 PM. These children observed, in the night sky, a luminous, blue, ovoid mass (30 cm at arm's length) with holes from which less bright blue lights emerged, varying in intensity and turning orange. This mass moved rapidly in a pendulum-like motion and remained stationary. After 10 seconds of observation, a blue flash appeared, followed by a series of flashes. This mass lit up and went out every 5 seconds. Another witness described the object as seen from a different location and angle, suggesting it was flying over the valley. The children will be interviewed by the Gendarmerie in the presence of their parents, but the testimonies will not be officially recorded. The present testimony is particularly strange: a completely luminous blue object with "holes" from which bright blue lights changed to orange. An object that switched on and off every 5 seconds; - 30 cm in size, measured at arm's length (that's 30 meters wide if you're 70 meters away!); - a pendular, undulating movement, flashes that didn't touch the ground... But this isn't a witness statement, but a description by a third party of sightings that weren't the subject of any direct testimony to the police or GEIPAN. The police simply announce that the children who made the observation confirm their statements as reported. This is quite different from a statement (and answer to a question) given by each of them and transcribed by a police officer. These days, GEIPAN doesn't take indirect witness statements into account. An indirect witness statement can't be considered reliable because the information is often insufficient and, above all, unreliable. In this particular case, given the unusual nature of the case, it would have required a good level of consistency to be usable (see the information on the GEIPAN classification methodology). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: unusable testimony.

summary: Observation of a bright point changing color: astronomical mistake with the star Capella.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, originally classified as type C, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This particular case study was classified as type C in 1991 by SEPRA and was previously named JEGUN (32) after the gendarmerie brigade. On August 6, 1991, at 12:15 AM, the gendarmerie in Jegun (32) was notified by a couple living in Saint-Lary (32) of a peculiar light in the sky. The station officer also observed the phenomenon from 12:35 AM and meticulously observed it with binoculars until 1:29 AM. This case is consistent (three witnesses, including a gendarme), and the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, size, color) with a well-known astronomical object: Capella. Furthermore, this star has a color perfectly consistent with that of the UFO. It is not the visual perception of the witnesses that is the issue, but rather their interpretation of their observation through their feelings (astonishment, fatigue, nighttime observation). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misidentification of the star Capella.

summary: Observation of a red sphere moving at high speed.
description: On August 5, 1991, at approximately 2:20 a.m., two gendarmes on patrol observed a red sphere about 80 cm in diameter moving very quickly and silently about fifteen meters above the ground. The phenomenon lasted very briefly. The statements of the two gendarmes are consistent, and the phenomenon could not be identified.

summary: Probable observation of laser beams from a disco projector.
description: witness reports that in mid-August 1991, around 10:30 PM, they saw a series of bright white dots moving erratically across the sky. These dots, high in the sky, suddenly formed a display, organizing themselves into various geometric shapes. This lasted approximately five minutes before the group coalesced into a point and disappeared, leaving a brief phosphorescent trail. This person likely witnessed the short-lived operation of a nightclub laser projector, which typically produces this type of formation in the sky. The witness also indicated that a nightclub in a nearby village has this type of equipment.

summary: Observation of a very bright white phenomenon the size of a small tourist plane
description: On July 23rd at approximately 11:30 AM, a witness observed a very bright and silent white phenomenon, about the size of a small private plane, lasting for about 15 seconds. No further information is available.

summary: Brief observations of the rapid and silent passage of 2 very bright colored discs in the sky of New Caledonia: very probable observations of a meteoroid reentry.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named LA FOA (988) 19.04.1991, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On April 19, 1991, around 5:00-5:30 PM, three witnesses were at the summit of an unwooded plateau near the Col d'Amieu pass in the municipality of Sarramea, New Caledonia. They suddenly observed the passage of two luminous phenomena in the clear sky. Despite their brief observations (from 2 to 3 seconds for T1 and T2) to about ten seconds (for T3), they described a circular phenomenon ("discs," "round shape," "ball"), with varying colors (T1 "silver," T2 "fluorescent green," and T3 "blue, pink, fluorescent green") moving silently along a straight east-west trajectory. The witnesses lost sight of the phenomenon, which was hidden by trees. T1 suspected the disintegration of a satellite. The police investigation ruled out an aircraft theft. While not particularly unusual, this case, with its relatively strong evidence (3 witnesses, fairly precise testimonies), appears to be very likely an observation of a meteor reentry (see the investigation report). The description of the UFO provided by the witnesses is indeed characteristic of this type of phenomenon: very rapid movement of two luminous objects, observation duration of 2 to 3 seconds. This conclusion is much more Easier today than it was 27 years ago. GEIPAN has since accumulated many testimonies, and nowadays several websites record reports of natural meteoroid re-entries. These re-entries can be observed during the day, with one or more flashes (fragmentation), with or without sound. The case of April 8, 2018, recorded in the USA, is one example among others of cases similar to that of our witnesses. It was during the day, there were several observers, several flashes (fragmentation), no trails, no sound (see the example on the website IMO). The short duration of the observation, as well as the east-to-west trajectory, argues against a possible satellite re-entry. This has also been confirmed by the absence of any recorded artificial re-entries. This case could correspond. It is class A: observation of a meteoroid reentry is very probable.

summary: Observation of lights arranged in a triangle in the sky: lack of information.
description: witness in a car observed three lights arranged in a triangle in the sky. This phenomenon was accompanied by a continuous humming sound. No other witnesses or further information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of a point of light larger than a star: lack of information.
description: On March 6, 1991, a witness observed a bright point of light larger than a star. The explanation of a laser from a nearby nightclub could not be considered, as the establishment was closed that day. No other information could be gathered.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry
description: Two independent witnesses observed an intense ball of light that crashed into the sea with a loud noise like an explosion. This was likely an atmospheric reentry, but it is impossible to determine whether it was natural or artificial.

summary: Periodic observation of a point of light: lack of information.
description: A witness observed a bright light from their home. This observation was repeated several days in a row around 9 PM. No further information is available.
